props.title: Site progress reported daily, not reconstructed monthly
props.lede: AI agents for contractors and builders that turn a site engineer's voice note into the daily progress report, follow every material order to the gate and keep subcontractors, drawings and costs in step. They work from WhatsApp on site and your ERP in the office.

intro.title: What does Exyconn build for construction?
intro.definition: is a set of agents that collects progress, material, safety and labour updates from site in whatever form they arrive, and turns them into the reports, orders and alerts your project team needs, so engineers spend less time typing and more time on the work. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents on WhatsApp for the site, and on your ERP, project schedule and drawing register for the office. Engineers and project managers still approve every quantity, drawing answer and payment.

benefits.title: Why contractors are doing this now

items.text: Every site supervisor already sends photos and voice notes on WhatsApp. The information exists; it just never reaches a report.
A day lost waiting for steel, a crane or an answer to an RFI pushes everything behind it on the schedule.
Clients, lenders and inspectors expect safety records that are written on the day, not filled in before an audit.
Labour and subcontractor gangs move between sites. Knowing who is where tomorrow is a daily phone exercise.
Margins on fixed-price work are thin. Overruns found at month end are too late to fix.

demo.title: whatsapp · site reporting
demo.caption: A site engineer sends a voice note and photos at the end of the shift; the agent drafts the daily progress report and flags a material shortfall.

messages.text: (voice note) 4th floor slab shuttering done in grid C to F, reinforcement 60% done. 42 labour today, 6 from Sharma's gang absent. TMT 12mm running short.
Thanks Imran. Draft DPR for Tower 2: shuttering complete grids C–F, reinforcement about 60%, manpower 42 against 48 planned. Is the slab pour still planned for Thursday?
Yes if steel comes by Wednesday
Stores shows 1.8 tonnes of 12mm on hand against about 3 tonnes still needed for the slab. The open PO with the supplier is due Thursday. Shall I ask purchase to expedite it to Wednesday morning?
Done. Purchase and the project manager have been told, and the DPR with your 9 photos is in their inbox for sign-off.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a project team's hours actually go
props.lede: Ask a project manager what slows a site down and it is rarely the concrete. It is information arriving late.

items.title: Daily reports typed up at night
items.text: Engineers spend the evening turning notebooks and WhatsApp photos into the DPR. When they're too tired, it is skipped and rebuilt from memory before the client meeting.

items.title: Materials chased by phone
items.text: Indents, purchase orders, GRNs and e-way bills sit in different hands. Nobody can say quickly whether the cement for Friday's pour has left the plant.

items.title: Safety paperwork that lags the work
items.text: Toolbox talks, permits for work at height and near-miss reports are filled on paper, if at all, and are hard to find when an inspector or client asks.

items.title: Subcontractors out of sequence
items.text: The plumber arrives before the slab is cured, the painter waits for the electrician. Each gang is coordinated by separate calls from the site.

items.title: Questions waiting on drawings
items.text: Site teams work from revised drawings, specifications and BOQ items spread across email and folders. An RFI can sit with the consultant for days while work stops.

items.title: Cost overruns found at month end
items.text: Actual quantities, labour bills and material consumption are compared with the BOQ and budget only when the RA bill is prepared, after the money is spent.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your team's plate

items.title: Daily site reports by voice and photo
items.text: Site engineers send a voice note and photos on WhatsApp in any language. The agent turns them into the DPR with progress by activity, manpower and equipment, and files it to the project for sign-off.

items.title: Material procurement and tracking
items.text: Raises indents from site requests, follows the purchase order and e-way bill with the supplier, records receipts against the GRN in your ERP and warns the site when stock won't cover the next activity.

items.title: Safety checks and incidents
items.text: Runs the daily checklist and toolbox talk record in chat, logs near-misses and incidents with photos and location, and alerts the safety officer at once. Investigations and corrective actions stay with your safety team.

items.title: Subcontractor scheduling
items.text: Shares the look-ahead plan from your project schedule with each subcontractor, confirms gangs and start dates, and tells the planner when a delay upstream means a trade should be held back.

items.title: Drawings and RFI answers
items.text: Finds the latest revision of a drawing, the specification clause or the BOQ item a site team asks about, and drafts RFIs for anything not covered. Design answers come only from the architect or consultant.

items.title: Cost versus budget
items.text: Compares quantities executed, material consumed and labour bills with the BOQ and budget each week, by package and by site, and highlights overruns while they can still be acted on.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day on a G+12 residential tower
props.lede: Follow a working Tuesday on site. Each moment lights the part of the project the agent is working on.

moments.title: The toolbox talk is on record
moments.text: The safety supervisor sends a photo of the morning talk and ticks the scaffold checklist in chat. A loose guard rail on level 9 is logged and the safety officer is alerted.

moments.title: The electrician is held back a day
moments.text: Blockwork on level 7 is running late. The agent tells the electrical subcontractor to start conduit work on Thursday instead and updates the look-ahead.

moments.title: A question about a lintel
moments.text: The foreman asks which lintel detail applies to the shaft opening. The agent finds it on revision R3 of the structural drawing; a second query on a clash is sent to the consultant as an RFI.

moments.title: Ready-mix for Thursday, confirmed
moments.text: The supplier confirms the concrete for the level 8 pour. The truckload of steel arrives, its e-way bill is matched and the GRN is recorded in the ERP.

moments.title: The DPR writes itself
moments.text: The site engineer sends a two-minute voice note and twelve photos on the way out. The draft DPR is with the project manager before he leaves the site office.

moments.title: Costs against the BOQ
moments.text: This week's reinforcement consumption is running ahead of the BOQ quantity for level 7. The weekly cost note to the project director flags it with the drawings involved.

items.question: Will this replace our site engineers or planners?
items.answer: No. It does the typing, chasing and searching so engineers and planners spend their time on the work and the decisions. Quantities, drawings, safety findings and payments are always approved by a named person.

items.question: Our site teams aren't comfortable with new apps. Will they use it?
items.answer: They don't need a new app. Site teams use WhatsApp, voice notes and photos as they do today, in Hindi, English or their regional language, and the agent does the structuring.

items.question: Which systems does it connect to?
items.answer: Your ERP or accounting system for purchase and GRNs, your project schedule in Primavera, MS Project or a spreadsheet, and the folders or document control system where drawings live. In the first week we confirm what each one exposes and what the agent can read or write.

items.question: Can the AI answer technical questions from site?
items.answer: It finds what is already in your approved drawings, specifications and BOQ and quotes the revision it used. If the documents don't answer the question, it drafts an RFI for the architect or consultant. It never makes a design or structural call.

items.question: How is project and worker data protected?
items.answer: Data stays in your systems and an environment set up for your firm, with role-based access by project and an audit log of every message. Worker details are handled under India's DPDP Act 2023, or the GDPR where it applies.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on the number of sites, users and systems. Most firms start with daily reports on one or two sites. Share your DPR format and we'll send a fixed quote for the first phase.
